title: The Green Lady's Island
synopsis: Otto says he was on Liberty Island when the bird was taken.
His sister sells postcards there, under the great statue.
Is his story true, and if not Otto, then who?
goal: Check Otto's morning, clear or catch him, and find who else knew about the bench.

options.label: Otto goes back to the bridge

notes: Letter: Otto's ferry ticket, the timetable and his sister's words. 'Otto goes back to the bridge' is a decoy: nobody says he did.

clueInputs.note: Otto's diary: the 9:30 ferry to Liberty Island.

learning.objective: 배표와 시간표(leaves at 9:30, takes fifteen minutes)를 읽고 오토의 오전을 순서대로 놓는다.
expressions: as soon as his boat arrived

play.title: Otto's Morning
story: The ferry crosses the harbor in the wind.
The Statue of Liberty grows bigger and bigger.
Otto's sister waves from her postcard stand.
play.letterIntro: Otto's ticket, the timetable and his sister say:
play.letter:
TICKET: Battery Park to Liberty Island. The boat leaves at 9:30 AM.
TIMETABLE: The trip takes fifteen minutes.
SISTER: "Otto came to my stand as soon as his boat arrived.
We ate lunch together at noon."
OTTO: "I sat on the bench half an hour before my boat."
play.question: Put Otto's Sunday morning in order.
hints: Half an hour before 9:30 is the earliest time.
Does anyone say Otto went back to the bridge?
transition: 9:00, the bench. 9:30, the boat. 9:45, the island. Noon, lunch.
"He never left my stand," his sister says.
"Look, I took a photo of him with a seagull at ten!"
play.orderFeedback: Find the earliest time first. Then follow the boat.

clue.title: Otto's Morning
clue.note: Otto was on the boat at 9:30 and on Liberty Island from 9:45 until lunch.

evidence.name: Otto's Ferry Ticket
evidence.description: Otto's ferry ticket from Battery Park to Liberty Island.

discovery.title: ON THE ISLAND AT 9:45
discovery.detail: Otto's ticket and his sister tell the same story.

notes: Letter: Maya's notes put the theft window (Case 04) beside Otto's morning, and define the word: proof you were in another place.

clueInputs.note: The bird was taken between 9:30 and 11:30.
Otto was on the boat and the island from 9:30.

learning.objective: 정의(proof that you were in another place)를 읽고 alibi라는 단어를 쓴다.
expressions: When you can prove you were in another place, you have an alibi.

play.title: Otto's Alibi
story: Otto's sister shows you her photo.
Otto, a seagull on his hat, the statue behind him.
Maya writes fast in her notebook.
play.letter:
The bird was taken between 9:30 and 11:30.
Otto's boat left at 9:30.
From 9:45 until noon, he was with his sister on the island.
His boots have no stars.
When you can prove you were in another place, you have an alibi.
play.question: What does Otto have now?
hints: Read the last line. It tells you the word.
Otto can prove he was on the island. What is that called?
transition: Otto was on the island while the paint was wet.
He did not take the brass bird.
Otto lets out a long breath. "Thank you."

feedback.EXCUSE: An excuse is just a reason. Otto has proof he was in another place.
feedback.TICKET: The ticket is part of the proof. What is all the proof called?

play.orderFeedback: Check your spelling: it is the word in the last line.

clue.title: Otto's Alibi
clue.value: ON THE ISLAND WHILE THE PAINT WAS WET
clue.note: Otto was on Liberty Island from 9:45. He did not take the bird.

evidence.name: The Seagull Photo
evidence.description: Otto's sister's photo of him on Liberty Island, a seagull on his hat.
evidence.inscription: Sunday, 10 AM. Otto and a seagull.

lines.text: I was grumpy. I am sorry.
I only wanted Eleanor's bird to come home.
Then help us find who took it.

discovery.title: NOT OTTO
discovery.detail: Otto has an alibi. Someone else was at the bench in star boots.

options.label: Mrs. Lee
options.feedback: Mrs. Lee never leaves her shop on Sundays.

options.label: Otto
options.feedback: Otto was not at the tea house. And he has an alibi.

notes: Letter: Maya's list of who heard the tin note (Case 03). Only the TV crew is left; Dexter said they would film the bridge.

clueInputs.note: The tin note named the bench; the TV crew filmed it.

learning.objective: 차 가게에서 쪽지를 들은 사람 목록을 읽고, 알리바이가 없는 사람을 남긴다.
expressions: She never leaves her shop on Sundays.
They said they would film the bridge.

play.title: Who Heard the Note?
story: You sit on a bench by the water.
"Only a few people heard the tin note," Maya says.
play.letter:
Who heard the tin note at the tea house?
Mrs. Lee. She never leaves her shop on Sundays.
Maya and the detective. We were at the library on Sunday morning.
Dexter Vance and Nora Bell, the TV crew.
They said they would film the bridge.
play.question: Who could have reached the bench first?
hints: Cross out each person who was somewhere else.
Who said they would go to the bridge?
play.successMessage: You found who could have done it!
transition: Only the TV crew is left on the list.
"But Dexter is so nice on TV!" Maya says.
"And Nora looked so worried at the tea house."

clue.title: The TV Crew
clue.note: Only Dexter Vance and Nora Bell heard the tin note and have no alibi.

evidence.name: Maya's List
evidence.description: Maya's list of who heard the tin note at the tea house.
evidence.inscription: Dexter Vance and Nora Bell, the TV crew.

discovery.title: THE TV CREW
discovery.detail: Dexter and Nora heard the tin note. Where were they on Sunday morning?

notes: Otto remembers the three notes on the bird's wing because their letter names spell the thing Grace gave you (the brass egg, Case 02): E, G, G. The first half of the song, paid off in Case 12.

clueInputs.note: Grace gave you the brass egg.
The first three notes are on the brass bird.

learning.objective: 음표에는 A부터 G까지 글자 이름이 있다는 설명을 읽고, 그랜드 센트럴에서 받은 물건(EGG)으로 세 음을 맞춘다.
expressions: Music notes have letter names, from A to G.
the thing Grace gave you at Grand Central

play.title: The Notes on the Wing
story: Otto takes a small notebook from his sister's stand.
"My grandfather's pocket book. It has a letter lock."
"Karl drew Eleanor's bird in it. With the notes on its wing."
play.letter:
I said hello to that bird every Sunday.
Three notes are carved on its wing.
Music notes have letter names, from A to G.
These three notes spell a word:
the thing Grace gave you at Grand Central.
Karl's book opens with that word.
play.question: Spell the three notes on the bird's wing.
hints: What did Grace give you at the Lost and Found?
Look at your Notebook: it was made of brass.
transition: Karl's drawing shows the bird and its wing: E, G, G.
"The song's first half," Maya says. "The thief has it too."
"Then we need the second half," says Otto. "Eleanor's family."
play.orderFeedback: The three tiles fit. What did Grace give you?

evidence.name: Karl's Pocket Book
evidence.description: Karl's small notebook, with his drawing of Eleanor's brass bird.
evidence.inscription: The notes on the wing: E, G, G.

ending.text: E, G, G. Now we know the song's first half.
ending.speaker: maya_chen

ending.text: The other half is with Eleanor's family.
And the thief is not me. Find the TV people!
ending.speaker: otto_brandt

ending.text: Across the water, Times Square's lights begin to shine.

hook: Otto is cleared. Where were Dexter Vance and Nora Bell on Sunday morning?

learningGoal.title: Times, a timetable and an alibi

objectives: Find out if Otto has an alibi.
intro: Liberty Island, in New York Harbor.
The Statue of Liberty holds her torch high.
Otto's sister sells postcards here every day.
play.caseSummary: Otto's boat left at 9:30. He reached the island at 9:45 and stayed until lunch. The bench paint was wet then, so Otto has an alibi. Only the TV crew heard the tin note and has no alibi. Karl's book gave the song's start: E, G, G.

notes: The red herring is cleared by evidence: Otto's ticket, the timetable, his sister and his plain boots against the wet-paint window.
E, G, G (s4_ep06_e4) is the song's first half, paid off in Case 12. Maya's list (s4_ep06_c3) turns the case toward the TV crew in Case 07.
